title: The ocean beneath a place: currents and temperature by depth, from the US Navy's global ocean model (HYCOM, ESPC-D-V02, 1/12 degree), analyses and forecast
provider: US Navy Fleet Numerical Meteorology and Oceanography Center (ESPC-D-V02, HYCOM ocean component), through HYCOM.org's THREDDS server

lat.description: latitude of the place (degrees north); the nearest grid point is taken

start.description: first time (UTC), moved down to a multiple of step_hours

end.description: last time (UTC); the forecast reaches about a week ahead

step_hours.description: hours between the times taken (the model's step is 3 h)

max_depth.description: deepest level taken (m); the 40 levels reach 5000 m

kuroshio.description: the Kuroshio south of Japan, as an example

on_demand.description: currents and temperature by depth beneath a chosen place, two days back and four ahead

format: One netCDF classic file per variable, dimensions (time, depth): water_u and water_v, eastward and northward sea-water velocity (m s-1); water_temp, sea-water temperature (degC). Coordinates: time and run (the forecast reference time of each time), seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC; depth (m, positive down; 40 levels from 0 to 5000 m). Global attributes give the grid point's latitude and longitude. Below the sea floor values are missing.
coverage: Global ocean from 80 S to 90 N on a 1/12 degree grid (0.08 degrees in longitude, 0.04 in latitude), 3-hourly; the best time series runs from about ten days back to seven days ahead
licence: Approved for public release; distribution unlimited (DoD Distribution A), provided as is (https://www.hycom.org). HYCOM.org asks for this acknowledgement: funding for the development of HYCOM has been provided by the National Ocean Partnership Program and the Office of Naval Research; data assimilative products using HYCOM are funded by the U.S. Navy; computer time was made available by the DoD High Performance Computing Modernization Program; the output is publicly available at https://hycom.org.
citation: Barton, N., Metzger, E. J., Reynolds, C. A., et al. (2021), The Navy's Earth System Prediction Capability: a new global coupled atmosphere-ocean-sea ice prediction system designed for daily to subseasonal forecasting, Earth and Space Science 8, e2020EA001199; data from HYCOM.org (ESPC-D-V02).
